body.x: INTHETECH (CEO Seung-Ho Choun) challenges the CES 2027 Innovation Awards with its webcam-based dual-task cognitive rehabilitation platform ‘EYAS Dual’. The company is a digital healthcare specialist enterprise developing AI digital therapeutics (DTx) and cognitive rehabilitation solutions.

Focusing on its eye-tracking technology-based cognitive rehabilitation software series ‘EYAS’, INTHETECH earned recognition for its technological capability and clinical validity by winning a CES 2026 Innovation Award. Domestically, the company supplies and operates cognitive rehabilitation solutions across more than 300 medical, public health, and specialized institutions—including major university hospitals, public health centers, dementia care centers, and child development centers—while exporting products to 14 countries including India, Thailand, Malaysia, Australia, Russia, and Canada.

As approximately 55 million people worldwide have dementia and about 10 million new cases develop each year, demand for cognitive rehabilitation expands beyond hospitals into local communities and homes. However, conventional digital rehabilitation devices remain confined to seated ‘finger training’ on touch screens, lacking physical participation and real-life transfer. At the same time, costs and space burdens of specialized equipment, alongside mid-program dropouts, have been pointed out as limitations.

body.cap: Cognitive rehabilitation training program screen of ‘EYAS Dual’ | Image provided by INTHETECH

body.x: EYAS Dual directly targets this issue as a next-generation dual-task cognitive rehabilitation platform. Featuring a ‘dual-task’ structure performing physical exercise and cognitive training simultaneously, it recognizes multi-angle motions—including hand gestures, upper limb range of motion, full-body balance, facial expressions, and voice responses—training in a manner where tasks are “solved only through movement.” It applies to dementia prevention, stroke rehabilitation, and child attention enhancement, aiming for real-life transfer connecting to daily activities such as grocery shopping, waste sorting, and refrigerator organization.

Its most notable feature is that it incurs no additional hardware purchasing costs. Operating immediately with standard PCs, tablets, or smartphones equipped with cameras without expensive dedicated sensors, it supports major operating systems including Web, Android, Windows, and macOS, significantly reducing adoption burdens for institutions. Furthermore, after measuring initial cognitive and motor levels through 6 standardized screening tests, it automatically prescribes 43 customized training programs and issues automatic reports containing response times, movement trajectories, and left-right asymmetry after sessions, delivering one-stop services from testing to prescription, training, and reporting. Inclusive designs—such as hand tremor compensation, flexible evaluations without incorrect answers, large fonts, and voice guidance—alongside adaptive difficulty levels tailored to user conditions reduce usage burdens and mid-program dropouts for elderly users and patients.

Building on these achievements and technologies, INTHETECH accelerates global market expansion. In India, the company established a local joint venture (JV), signed a 3-year supply contract targeting 8 major cities, and conducts empirical collaboration with local universities and institutions. In the Middle East, attracting investment from Qatar Development Bank (QDB), the company plans to establish a Middle East entity in Qatar this August to expand business across the GCC region using it as a hub. In North America, pursuing US FDA approval procedures, the company targets medical institutions and rehabilitation markets led by EYAS Dual, which requires no hardware, while preparing entry into Northern Europe, including Finland. Participating in international exhibitions like MEDICA in Germany and WHX in Dubai alongside its CES 2026 Innovation Award win, the company aims to expand export destinations to over 20 countries.

An official from INTHETECH stated, “While conventional digital rehabilitation was limited to sitting down and touching screens, EYAS Dual stimulates the body and cognition simultaneously through a structure where tasks are solved only when moving the body.” The official added, “Because it can be used immediately with just a webcam, significantly lowering adoption barriers, we will present a new standard for cognitive rehabilitation in North American, European, and Middle Eastern markets using CES 2027 as a stepping stone.”
